chunks: In the name of God, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.
From Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), that he said:
When the month of Ramadan comes, recite Inna Anzalnahu one thousand times every night.
Then, when the night of the twenty-third arrives, strengthen your heart and open your ears to the hearing of the wonders you will witness.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Opening words of Surah al-Qadr (97:1), the chapter about Laylat al-Qadr
key_terms.الْعَجَائِب: Wonders, extraordinary signs and phenomena that descend on the Night of Power
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ ثَلَاثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ: The night of the twenty-third of Ramadan, a candidate for Laylat al-Qadr in Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about reciting Surah al-Qadr in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to recite Surah al-Qadr (Inna Anzalnahu) one thousand times each night of Ramadan. On the night of the twenty-third — believed in Shia tradition to be among the nights of Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Divine Decree — he exhorts heightened spiritual attentiveness: to steel the heart and open the ears to behold the extraordinary signs and manifestations that descend that night. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on the 23rd night of Ramadan as one of the holiest nights.
